reviews.review_title: Review at Baoz Dimsum - Nguyễn Tri Phương
reviews.review_text:
Peter H
Philadelphia, United States17 contributions
0
Locals, not tourist
Nov 2022
When visiting cities, we enjoy walking and exploring. On this day, we set out on a mission to see a bit of the city and find dim sum for lunch. Having walked from District 1 to District 5, we found Baoz Dim Sum. 
We were the only tourist in the restaurant on a Wednesday morning/afternoon. Otherwise, the place was filled with locals.
In reading some of the other reviews, I would say that everything is relative based on your past experience and expectations.
The service was very good on our visit. While I do not speak Vietnamese, the dim sum menu has everything written in Vietnamese, Chinese and English. Fortunately, our server did speak Cantonese and that was helpful for me. Otherwise, I feel that her English would have been good enough too!
If you are seeking a dim sum restaurant with carts, this is not the place. You order off of a menu and the items are cooked to order which affords hot and fresh dim sum.
We had shrimp and chive dumplings, rice noodles with shrimp, shui mai, baked BBQ pork buns and steam sticky rice in bamboo leaves. All of the items were hot and tasted very good. The dough for the baked BBQ pork buns is a bit different as it was not as fluffy as we are used to and it's a bit sweeter.
Some of the reviews here state that the restaurant is pricey and/or not a good price-value meal. Again, everything being relative, I felt that it was a great bargain. 5-dim sum dishes with tea for two cost us $15USD. To me, that's cheap eats for good food.
This restaurant is in District 5 and it is surrounded by small shops, local market and away from tourist. If you are in the area, it's well worth a visit for HK style dim sum.
